content.text: Confirmed across confidentiality and transition sections too — no personnel-restriction covenant exists. Resubmitting the finding with the deterministic-check reasoning made explicit.

input.quote: Nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling, or using any product or service, engaging any supplier, hiring any person who responds to general recruitment, or conducting business in any field or territory. Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment.
input.rationale: Compliant at the PREFERRED position: no non-solicit on Customer. Full-text searches for "solicit", "hire", "induce", "employ", "recruit" and "personnel", plus reads of General (§ 30), Customer Responsibilities (§ 12), Confidentiality (§ 16) and Transition Assistance (§ 11), return no non-solicitation, no-poach or no-hire covenant binding Customer (or either Party). § 12.3 goes further than the playbook requires by affirmatively recording that Customer has made no no-hire (or exclusivity/non-compete) commitment and stays free to hire any person responding to general recruitment. The fallback-wording heuristics that flagged as failing — duration capped at 12 months and an express general-solicitation/unsolicited-approach carve-out — test the drafting of a restrictive covenant and are inapplicable here because there is no covenant to narrow; adding such language would import a restriction on us that does not currently exist. Accordingly no redline is proposed. § 12.4 (restricting Vendor from marketing a competing analytics service) is not flagged because it runs in our favour.
